epistemic_role: Deterministic phenomenological transition-interface falsification, not a D4 physical-kernel or performance experiment
question: Can an earlier public correction alter the next private projector state and public first record under a stipulated feedback kernel while a matched no-feedback null cannot?

research_basis.decision: Discussion thread-009 authorizes a D4 phenomenological/projector-level JIT translation and action-bound post-flux charge measurement, not microscopic transition probabilities.

sources.role: Lyons–Brown motivates active correction and ungauging of hidden anyons in D(S3), not a D4 numerical law.
Jing et al. formulate noisy-syndrome spacetime JIT; numerical performance and threshold proof remain open.

fixed_scope.geometry: One site, two ordered rounds, labels vacuum/m_flux/e_charge; structural unit fixture, not the L=2 physical code or a logical-error-rate trial.
fixed_scope.first_observation_timing: Round-0 full-binary first record (flux-syndrome and herald-membership bits) precedes any action; round-1 first record follows round-0 action and private transition. Online action sees no future record.
fixed_scope.second_record_timing: Commit yields the full-binary public [charge=0,vacuum=1] report bound to the exact public action digest; defer has no second-stage measurement. The second-exogenous key selects the private charge outcome but is not a policy input.
fixed_scope.action_binding: Compute SHA-256 over canonical sorted-key compact JSON of {round:0, action:<defer|commit>, first_record:<two-bit round-0 array>}; E2 carries exactly that digest and rejects any substituted digest.
fixed_scope.public_private_boundary: Policy sees only the causal full-binary first record and prior public transcript. Hidden labels, faults, transition rule, second-stage truth, winding and score remain private; public serialization has no support/pairing/truth fields.

kernel.no_feedback_null: For either action under the zero-fault fixture, next private label is m_flux with probability 1, other labels 0.
kernel.action_feedback_fixture: Defer gives next private label m_flux with probability 1; commit with the fixed vacuum second outcome gives vacuum with probability 1; other labels 0. This intervention table is stipulated solely for interface validation, not derived D4 fusion physics.

fixed_scope.private_score: Boolean union of terminal non-vacuum residual and ground-state-relative nontrivial-winding bit (fixed false). It is a fixture diagnostic, not code LER; no stochastic denominator is defined.

matrix: Exactly four unique model-by-action cells and one exact replay each. For causal invariance, in each cell toggle only the round-1 public flux-syndrome bit after action/E2, leaving the round-0 record and all three keys fixed; the round-0 action and E2 binding must remain unchanged. No other arm/rate/size is permitted.
acceptance: Upstream review hash/status pass; each categorical conditional kernel has nonnegative entries summing to 1 over vacuum/m_flux/e_charge.
All four cells share three exogenous keys and the round-0 public record; actions depend only on that record, not future or private truth.
Both models preserve round-0 public and action-bound commit E2; null has action-invariant next hidden/first record, feedback has action-sensitive next hidden/first record.
A future-only first-record perturbation cannot change earlier action or E2 binding; a wrong action digest fails E2 binding; public serialization excludes private data.
Private Boolean-union score matches each terminal private state and winding; exact replay matches all cells; no risk, LER, threshold, circuit-level or JIT-advantage claim is emitted.
stop_rule: Fail closed on hash/status, causality, binding, normalization, separation or replay mismatch. Do not change J6/J6B data or choose a D4 physical probability from this fixture.
claim_boundary: A pass validates only interface capacity for an action-to-future-state path under stipulated deterministic fixtures. The physically correct D4 action-conditioned kernel and schedule benefit remain unresolved.
